messages:
mike_infra: FYI scheduling a staged maintenance for the us-east2 GPU fleet to address NIC microcode and thermal-sensor firmware that intermittently drops RX under sustained KV-cache pressure.

mike_infra: Proposed window: 2026-04-06 01:00-04:00 UTC. We plan 8 cohorts (~90 GPUs each, ~4% pool) to keep per-cohort impact small. Each cohort: cordon 8m -> drain 5m -> reboot/power-cycle 7m -> post-checks 10m -> kv-warm 12m. Target ~42m per cohort.

sara_sre: Will we trigger automatic cross-region routing for hosted tenants? Concern about tail latency when chat traffic moves to eu/us regions.

mike_infra: Yes. Smart-routing will shift to compatible model variants in other regions. Expect p95 uplift; our estimate: 50-250ms depending on model and payload. Canary at 0.5% traffic, step to 5% after 15m if stable. Rollback thresholds: p95 +200ms OR errors >1%.

leo_ops: Need numbers for finance: estimated warmup token volume and cost. Also how many GPUs offline at once?

mike_infra: Peak ~90 GPUs per cohort offline. Warmup prefetch will replay common prefixes and warm KV entries. Estimate ~110k tokens per cohort (total ~880k). Cost rough: $25-$70 depending on model pathing and quantization. We'll capture exact token tally in the maintenance runbook.

anne_prod: Private/VPC customers affected? Do we need org-level emails or just UI banner?

mike_infra: Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem) unchanged. Hosted orgs with >0.5% of their traffic from us-east2 will get an email. We'll also post a banner in Console with UTC times and the fallback behavior. No API surface changes.

deploy-bot: maintenance scheduled: id=mm-20260406-ue2-01, start=2026-04-06T01:00Z, end=2026-04-06T04:00Z. Notifications: 48h, 2h, 15m.

jin_reliability: Please add me to the canary watch rotation. I'll own p95 and error-rate alarms and will have escalation path to infra on-call.

leo_ops: Also flag: last quarter we hit cross-region egress throttling during warmups. Suggest reserving bandwidth with cloud provider and kicking off warmup in a bandwidth-controlled manner. I'll open provider ticket.

mike_infra: Opened ticket INF-8011 with cloud provider for dedicated egress reservation and NIC firmware QA. Also creating runbook draft at /docs/maintenance/us-east2-nic-thermal-stabilization.md. Will include exact commands and command timeouts.

mike_infra: Sample warmup commands (run from staging controller):
```
# prefetch common prefixes into KV cache
infractl warmup --pool=us-east2-gpu --cohort=2 --input=common_prefixes.txt --concurrency=4
# cordon + drain
infractl cordon --pool=us-east2-gpu --cohort=2 --reason="nic-fw-thermal-fix"
infractl drain --pool=us-east2-gpu --cohort=2 --timeout=300
# reboot
infractl reboot --pool=us-east2-gpu --cohort=2 --type=powercycle
```

anne_prod: Can we include a short customer-facing blurb for the banner? Keep it simple and non-technical.

mike_infra: Draft blurb: "Planned maintenance in US-East region on 2026-04-06 01:00-04:00 UTC. We expect minimal disruption; some requests may be routed to nearby regions causing slightly higher latency. No action required." Will share in #announcements.

sara_sre: Canary watch checklist: verify p95 at per-route level, overall error-rate, token-drop anomalies, and KV hit-rate. If KV hit-rate drops >10% post-cohort, hold progression and investigate.

mike_infra: Added checklist to runbook. Progression policy: hold if any threshold breached or if cloud provider flags the cohort. Fallback: if issues persist after 2 cohorts, pause and escalate to firmware vendor.

leo_ops: I'll schedule provider support window and ask for temporary egress bump. Ticket INF-8011 linked to maintenance.

mike_infra: TL;DR: small cohorted reboots to fix NIC/thermal instability, canary at 0.5%, rollback on p95+200ms or errors>1%, private VPCs unaffected, banner+emails for affected orgs, runbook and postmortem will be attached to mm-20260406-ue2-01. :white_check_mark:
